titulo: Do you really have to wait to swim after eating?
destinatario: se lo manda un adulto joven al padre o la madre que lo hacía esperar sentado en la toalla después del almuerzo
regla_guardable: Swim after lunch if you feel up to it. The real pool risk is alcohol.
fuentes: American Red Cross Scientific Advisory Council (2011): no evidence that swimming after eating causes drowning
Scouting for Boys (1908): often cited as an early warning against bathing soon after meals (Mental Floss, WBUR; a historian disputes it)
CDC drowning risk factors (cdc.gov/drowning/risk-factors): alcohol linked to a large share of water-recreation deaths in teens and adults

frases.texto: You made your kids sit out the pool for thirty minutes after lunch.
frases.estilo: Dry, direct, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Researchers haven't found any digestion cramp that makes swimmers sink.
The idea was that your blood rushes to your stomach and leaves your arms and legs empty.
But in the research the Red Cross reviewed, swimming after eating didn't hold swimmers back.
The American Red Cross reviewed the research and found no evidence that swimming after eating causes drowning.
One early printed warning is often traced to a Boy Scouts handbook from nineteen oh eight.
Heads up: after a huge meal, you might get a side stitch.
Annoying, but nothing the research ties to drowning.
What does matter is alcohol. The CDC links it to a large share of teen and adult deaths around water.
Send this to the friend whose parents made them wait on the towel.
